data.title: User Journey
data.tagline: A staged view of a user's actions, thoughts, feelings, and obstacles across touchpoints while pursuing a goal
data.learningOutcome: You can organize stages, actions, touchpoints, thoughts, feelings, obstacles, and evidence, then distinguish a user journey from a user flow.
data.description: A learner might discover a course through a friend, visit its page, pay, receive an email, and enter the first lesson. A user journey needs interview or behavioral evidence and must not present team assumptions as real feelings.

learning.assumes: You can map an in-product task but have not connected discovery, purchase, use, and support touchpoints.
learning.outcome: You can organize stages, actions, touchpoints, thoughts, feelings, obstacles, and evidence, then distinguish a user journey from a user flow.

explanation.title: Start with one user and goal
explanation.text: Define the user, situation, and time span instead of mixing different people's experiences.

explanation.title: Connect touchpoints inside and outside the product
explanation.text: Social sharing, pages, payment, email, the app, and support may all affect one goal.

explanation.title: Separate evidence from assumptions
explanation.text: Interviews, feedback, and behavior data support claims; team guesses remain hypotheses.

data.boundary: A User Journey spans time and touchpoints with actions, thoughts, feelings, and evidence. A User Flow focuses on pages, actions, and decisions for one in-product goal.

lessonPractice.title: Which artifact is closest to the user journey for buying and starting a course?

options.label: Map discovery, evaluation, purchase, email, and course entry, with actions, questions, feelings, and interview or behavior evidence at each touchpoint
options.feedback: Correct. It spans time and touchpoints while connecting actions, thoughts, feelings, and evidence.

options.label: Show only the click branches between sign-in, the course list, and the player
options.feedback: That is closer to a user flow, which focuses on actions and decisions inside the product.

options.label: Write “users will definitely feel excited” without interviews, feedback, or behavior evidence
options.feedback: A journey can include feelings, but it must separate evidence, inference, and assumptions.

data.agentPrompt: Map the user journey for buying and starting a course for the first time across discovery, evaluation, purchase, notification, and first learning. For each stage, state the touchpoint, action, question, feeling, obstacle, and available evidence. Label interview quotes separately from behavioral data and mark unsupported claims as hypotheses. Identify the friction that needs more research without reducing the journey to an in-product user flow.
